thread:
Maya (acme): hey team — after a VPC peering change at ~02:30 UTC our internal service acme-api.prod.internal is returning NXDOMAIN from within our VPC. External users unaffected, but internal apps can't reach the endpoint. Anyone seen this pattern?

Sara (support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a quick dig/nslookup output and confirm the VPC ID + region? any infra changes besides the peering?

Maya (acme): we did a peering with analytics-vpc in us-west-2 at 02:30. dig from an app host:
```
$ dig +short acme-api.prod.internal

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> acme-api.prod.internal +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 45213
;; Query time: 2 msec
;; SERVER: 172.31.0.2#53(172.31.0.2)
```
no answer. nslookup points at the VPC resolver.

Alex (neteng): rough checklist — private hosted zone associations, Route53 resolver rules, and any duplicate private hosted zones in the customer's account that could shadow ours. Can you run: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name \"prod.internal\"` in your account and also from our account we can check hosted zone associations.

Maya (acme): running now, output:
```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "prod.internal"
{
  "HostedZones": [
    {
      "Id": "/hostedzone/Z2EXAMPLE123",
      "Name": "prod.internal.",
      "Config": {"PrivateZone": true},
      "ResourceRecordSetCount": 42
    }
  ]
}
```
We also have a private hosted zone in our account with same name created during migration last month.

route53-bot: Hosted zone Z2EXAMPLE123 is associated with VPCs: vpc-analytics-0a1b2c (in Account A), not vpc-acme-9f8e7d (customer account).

Chris (oncall): that smells like split-horizon / mis-association — if the hosted zone is associated only to analytics-vpc, DNS in the customer VPC will not see the records and will hit NXDOMAIN. Did the peering change cause the hosted zone association to be flipped or a new hosted zone created?

Fiona (sre): also check for duplicate hosted zone in the customer's account — AWS will prefer the zone in the same account/VPC and that can shadow our records with empty content. Maya, can you `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z2EXAMPLE123 | grep acme-api -A2` and paste results?

Maya (acme): run that now — result shows no acme-api record in Z2EXAMPLE123 (the one associated to analytics). In our account's hosted zone (different ID) there is a stub/placeholder CNAME that points to a private ELB but seems misconfigured.

Sara (support): summary so far: there are two private hosted zones with the same DNS name across accounts; the hosted zone with the real records is associated to analytics-vpc, while the customer VPC is either associated to a different (empty) zone or not associated at all. Peering change likely changed which resolver path the app uses.

Alex (neteng): repro steps for us: 1) from a host in customer VPC, `dig +trace acme-api.prod.internal` 2) `dig @172.31.0.2 acme-api.prod.internal` 3) check `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids vpc-acme-9f8e7d` and our `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z3REDWOOD456` to verify associations. Can someone paste dig +trace output?

Maya (acme): dig +trace shows that the request hits the VPC resolver but then returns NXDOMAIN; trace ends on our resolver IP.
```
;; Received 2 answers
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 56321
```

Chris (oncall): given the data, safe mitigation options: A) temporarily associate the correct hosted zone (Z3REDWOOD456) to the customer VPC so records resolve again (needs account VPC id + IAM approval), or B) coordinate with the customer to remove the duplicate/placeholder private hosted zone in their account. Option A is quickest but we should confirm cross-account association policies.

Fiona (sre): also verify there are no resolver rules in the customer account that forward the name to some forwarder that doesn't know about our records. `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=Name,Values=\"prod.internal\"` from both accounts.

Maya (acme): found a resolver rule in their account forwarding prod.internal to a forwarder IP that doesn't host our records. That got created during the migration. If the peering changed which path the resolver takes, that would explain intermittent failures.

Alex (neteng): ok that matches. Root cause likely: migration added a conditional forwarder in the customer's account and our hosted zone ended up associated to a different VPC (analytics). When traffic started using the forwarder path, the forwarder returned NXDOMAIN because it didn't have our records.

Sara (support): recommended remediation plan: 1) We temporarily associate Z3REDWOOD456 to vpc-acme-9f8e7d (will schedule for 10:30 UTC after security thumbs-up). 2) Customer to remove the placeholder private hosted zone and/or the resolver rule that forwards prod.internal to the forwarder. 3) After cleanup, disassociate any analytics-vpc-only associations that shouldn't be primary.

Chris (oncall): I can create the temporary association — I'll create a change ticket with the exact CLI: `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z3REDWOOD456 --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-acme-9f8e7d` (requires cross-account role).

Maya (acme): thanks — we'll remove the duplicate hosted zone and resolver rule once the temporary assoc is live and we verify resolution.

Fiona (sre): postmortem notes to capture: how peering changes affect resolver selection, prevent creation of duplicate private zones during migration (add check), and update runbook for cross-account hosted zone association.

Sara (support): quick verification steps once assoc is done: from a customer app host `dig +short acme-api.prod.internal` should return the private ELB CNAME/IP. then `curl -v https://acme-api.prod.internal/health` should succeed (TLS cert should match internal name or SNI).

Maya (acme): assoc completed at 10:40 UTC — DNS now resolves, health check passes. We'll leave the placeholder zone for 24h then delete. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Alex (neteng): great — leaving a note to automate a check for duplicate private hosted zones during tenant migrations.

Chris (oncall): closing out this thread after we confirm cleanup. If anything flips back, re-open and ping me.
